premises.text: Today's cost and tech trends can move robots from large, expensive, hard-to-use machines to personal home robots
premises.evidence_span: take this kind of robots, large, expensive, very difficult to use, and move them into engaging, affordable, and fun to use robots in the home

premises.text: Smartphone and cloud robotics make robots cheaper and automatically smarter as devices upgrade
premises.evidence_span: mostly smartphone robotics and cloud robotics that takes a computation from the robot into devices you already have, making it much more affordable, and also automatically and dynamically upgradable

premises.text: Narrow task robots priced for homes beat expensive do-everything robots
premises.evidence_span: Swiss army knife kind of robots that do anything from saving princesses to cleaning the house, but unfortunately cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. We're going to have a set of robots that are much more targeted at limited set of tasks

premises.text: Dumb robot smartphone approach: hardware is motors/speakers/power; behavior runs on phone app and cloud
premises.evidence_span: dumb robot smartphone approach. And everything that the robot does actually happens on a smartphone app and on the cloud. And the robot is just some motors, high-end speakers, and power

premises.text: Cloud beat/segment/genre data creates live song choreography on the Android device
premises.evidence_span: taking information from the cloud that has the beats, the segments, where the chorus starts, where the verse starts, what genre the song is. And it creates a real-time live choreography

premises.text: Camera face tracking aims the robot for better sound
premises.evidence_span: using the camera to track my faces, always pointing towards me and giving me the best sound possible

value.text: A robot in every home that is engaging, affordable, and fun
value.evidence_span: robot in every home and make it a reality

causal_links.evidence_span: engaging, affordable, and fun to use robots in the home

notes: Run2 merges product identity into the dumb-robot architecture premise (fewer than run1). Kickstarter early price treated as detail of the $199 commercial offer rather than a separate channel module. Singleton price domain retained.
